column1: # Expected verdicts for tests/fixtures/*.md — read by lint-runbooks.sh --self-test.
# Every fixture here is a shape that a previous version of the parser got
# WRONG, so each row is a regression test with a name. Columns:
#   fixture   exit   blocks   bad
# `exit` is the linter's status for that file alone, `blocks` the number of
# SHELL blocks it should find (a text or yaml block is tracked and skipped, not
# counted), `bad` how many of those should fail `bash -n`.
# All three are asserted, not just the exit status: a parser that stops
# counting text blocks still exits 1 on fixture-bad.md, for the wrong reason
# and with the wrong number of blocks. The counts are what notice that.
# --self-test requires a row for every fixture on disk and a fixture for every
# row, so adding one of the two without the other fails rather than passing
# quietly.
fixture-bad.md
fixture-htmlcomment.md
fixture-infostring.md
fixture-inlinecomment.md
fixture-longclose.md
fixture-nested.md
fixture-tilde.md
fixture-unterminated.md
